close_reason: Fixed in commit d0a0bd4. metadata_set's doc-comment now includes an explicit paragraph explaining the typed-update vs untyped-create asymmetry: PatchObject has one stable shape, whereas a Metadata create object is one of three @type variants with vendor extras at every level, so forcing it through a single Rust type would fight the spec's extensibility model. Mirrors the canonical mail-client email_set posture.
description: src/methods/metadata.rs:130 metadata_set takes create: Option<serde_json::Value>. PLAN.md §Method-specific Notes calls out that the canonical filter type is jmap_metadata_types::MetadataFilterCondition (which the metadata-types crate does export). The choice to make /set's create map opaque is defensible (the create-map keys are caller-chosen creation ids; the values are partial Metadata objects with no id), but contrast: jmap_types::PatchObject is used for update (typed), while create is untyped. Asymmetric on its face. Suggested rewrite: keep Value for create (documented rationale: creation ids are caller-chosen strings and the create values are partial Metadata, which the spec accepts as the JSON wire shape) but add a one-line doc-comment on metadata_set explaining the asymmetry to head off the obvious 'why is update typed but create untyped?' contributor question. Mirrors what mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:97 already does well.
title: metadata_set: filter/sort/create types are 'serde_json::Value' but PLAN.md describes them as typed
